title: Diagonal Argument Generalized to Regular Cardinals

problemStatement.formal: ∀ κ regular uncountable, ∀ f : ι → Ordinal, #ι < κ → (∀ i, f i < κ.ord) → ∃ β < κ.ord, ∀ i, f i < β
problemStatement.plain: Generalize the Cantor diagonal argument from ℵ₁ to arbitrary regular cardinals. The key property is regularity (cof = κ), not just uncountability.
whyMatters: Unifies all diagonal-type arguments under one theorem
The ℵ₁ case is a 3-line specialization

proven: regular_sup_bounded: iSup f < κ.ord for regular κ
card_succ_lt_of_lt_infinite: μ+1 < κ for infinite κ
regular_diagonal: main diagonal argument for regular κ

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: Generalized diagonal argument to all regular cardinals
insights: Regularity is the essential property — singular cardinals have countable cofinality
The proof factors cleanly into: bounded sup (regularity) + limit ordinal (infinite) + diagonal step
